instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put a large skillet over medium heat and toast the 10 guajillo chiles for about 15 seconds on each side, until they smell toasty.
Transfer the chiles into a saucepan, cover them with 3 cups of hot water, and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft.
Meanwhile, bring a medium pot of salted water to a boil. Peel the potatoes and carrots and cut both into 1/4 inch dice.
Boil the potatoes for 4 to 5 minutes. Add the carrots and boil for 3 to 4 minutes more, until both are tender but still firm. Drain and spread them on a plate to cool.
Chop 4 tsp of the onion and stir it into the queso fresco, crumbling the cheese as you go. Dice 4 of the radishes and slice 4 romaine leaves thinly.
Blend the softened chiles with 1 1/2 cups of the soaking liquid, the garlic, the oregano and 1/2 tsp of the salt until smooth.
Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in the large skillet over medium-high heat. Stand back and pour in the chile purée. It will spatter. Cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until it darkens.
Stir in the broth and cook for 2 minutes. Take the skillet off the heat and cover it to keep the sauce warm.
Whisk the vinegar, the olive oil, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, the pepper and a pinch of sugar in a bowl. Add the potatoes, carrots and diced radishes and toss.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a clean skillet over medium heat. Warm the tortillas a few at a time for about 15 seconds on each side and stack them under a towel.
Dip each tortilla in the warm sauce. Lay it on a baking sheet, put 2 tbsp of the cheese mixture down the middle, and fold it into a half moon. You'll have 12.
Spoon the rest of the sauce over the enchiladas. Bake for 10 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling at the edges.
Divide the sliced romaine among plates and set 3 enchiladas on each. Top with the potato and carrot mix and the remaining 1/2 cup cheese. Serve with the pickled jalapeños on the side.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version of this dish has 20 ratings, so the lead is the one that matches the dish as named: Hispanic Food Network's cheese enchiladas with a guajillo sauce, queso fresco filling, and boiled potatoes and carrots in a vinegar dressing (5.0 from 1 vote). Dora's Table (4.86 from 7) and Paulina Cocina (3.8 from 4) agree on the guajillo sauce, the dipped corn tortillas and the potato and carrot topping; Dora's fills with mushrooms and Paulina's fries the vegetables. The lead's 15 chiles and 1 1/2 cups of chicken broth are cut to 10 chiles and vegetable broth, the vegetables go down to a lighter dressing, and the sauce is not strained. The list says 12 tortillas and 1 lb each of potatoes and carrots, which the lead leaves out and Dora's gives.
